source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 6 (a)-(d): swing h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2 sin(3 pi t); maximum, minimum, period, first time at 2.12 m. Answer key PDF 309.

blocks.prompt: 6 A child is playing on a swing in a playground. The height \(h(t)\) of the swing seat above the ground (in meters) at time \(t\) (in seconds) is modeled by the function: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\). (a) What is the maximum height reached by the swing seat?
blocks.explanation:
Largest value of \(a + b\sin(\ldots)\) with \(a = 1.5\), \(b = 1.2\).
Plan: sine is at most 1.
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\).
To find: the maximum of \(h\).
Method: \(\sin(3\pi t) \le 1\), and \(b = 1.2 > 0\), so the maximum is \(a + b\).

Use the largest sine
\[\sin(3\pi t) = 1\]
\[h = 1.5 + 1.2(1) = 2.7\]
Why: The plus sign means \(h\) is largest when sine is largest.

When it happens
\[3\pi t = \tfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = \tfrac{1}{6} \text{ s}\]
Why: Sine is 1 at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\); divide by \(3\pi\).

Check
\[h\left(\tfrac{1}{6}\right) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin\tfrac{\pi}{2} = 2.7 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The value is actually reached.

blocks.prompt: 6 A child is playing on a swing in a playground. The height \(h(t)\) of the swing seat above the ground (in meters) at time \(t\) (in seconds) is modeled by the function: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\). (b) What is the minimum height reached by the swing seat?
blocks.explanation:
Smallest value of the same function.
Plan: sine is at least \(-1\).
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\).
To find: the minimum of \(h\).
Method: \(\sin(3\pi t) \ge -1\), so the minimum is \(a - b\).

When it happens
\[3\pi t = \tfrac{3\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ s}\]
Why: Sine is \(-1\) at \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\).

Check
\[0.3 > 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The seat stays above the ground, as a real swing must.

blocks.prompt: 6 A child is playing on a swing in a playground. The height \(h(t)\) of the swing seat above the ground (in meters) at time \(t\) (in seconds) is modeled by the function: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\). (c) How long does it take for the swing to complete one full back-and-forth motion (period)?
blocks.explanation:
One full back-and-forth motion is one period of the sine.
Plan: period of \(\sin(ct)\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{c}\).
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\), so \(c = 3\pi\).
To find: the period.
Method: \(\sin\theta\) repeats every \(2\pi\); \(\sin(ct)\) repeats when \(ct\) grows by \(2\pi\).

Use the period formula
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3\pi} = \dfrac{2}{3} \text{ s}\]
Why: The \(\pi\) cancels.

Check
\[h\left(t + \tfrac{2}{3}\right) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t + 2\pi)\]
\[= h(t) \;\checkmark\]
Why: Adding \(\frac{2}{3}\) s adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle.

blocks.prompt: 6 A child is playing on a swing in a playground. The height \(h(t)\) of the swing seat above the ground (in meters) at time \(t\) (in seconds) is modeled by the function: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\). (d) At what time(s) does the swing seat first reach a height of 2.12 meters?
blocks.explanation:
Solve \(h(t) = 2.12\) for the smallest positive \(t\).
Plan: isolate the sine, use inverse sine (in radians), divide by \(3\pi\).
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t)\), \(h(t) = 2.12\).
To find: the first \(t > 0\) with this height.
Method: Undo the formula: subtract 1.5, divide by 1.2, then \(\sin^{-1}\).

Get the sine alone
\[1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi t) = 2.12\]
\[1.2\sin(3\pi t) = 0.62\]
\[\sin(3\pi t) = 0.5167\]
Why: Subtract 1.5, then divide by 1.2.

Inverse sine
\[3\pi t = \sin^{-1}(0.5167)\]
\[\approx 31.11^{\circ} = 0.5430 \text{ rad}\]
Why: The smallest positive angle gives the first time; \(3\pi t\) is in radians.

The other time in the first swing
\[3\pi t = \pi - 0.5430 = 2.5986\]
\[t \approx 0.276 \text{ s}\]
Why: Sine is also positive in Quadrant II, so the seat passes 2.12 m again on the way down; then the pattern repeats every \(\frac{2}{3}\) s.

Check
\[1.5 + 1.2\sin(3\pi \times 0.0576)\]
\[= 1.5 + 1.2(0.5167) = 2.12 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Substituting gives the required height.
blocks.final_answer: First at \(t \approx 0.058\) s (going up); again at \(t \approx 0.276\) s (coming down)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints 0.05 second. The correct value is \(t = \frac{\sin^{-1}(0.5167)}{3\pi} = \frac{0.5430}{9.4248} = 0.0576\) s, which rounds to 0.058 s (0.06 s to two decimal places), not 0.05 s.
